validity.researcher_notes: Per Wikipedia (Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline), the ~785 km Pakistani segment runs through Balochistan and Sindh; at Khuzdar 'a branch would spur off to Karachi, while the main pipeline would continue towards Multan' -- i.e. Karachi is a genuine, sourced branch endpoint of this project's Pakistani leg, distinct from the main trunk that was to continue toward Multan and, in the original never-realized IPI concept, on to Delhi/India. Times of Islamabad (2026-06-16) corroborates that the Pakistani segment runs 'about 781 kilometres from the border through Balochistan to connect with the national gas grid' -- Karachi/Sindh being the hub of that national grid (SSGC), consistent with a Karachi terminus/branch, though it does not name Karachi explicitly. India withdrew from the trilateral IPI project in 2009 and the Multan-to-Delhi extension was never built or mapped, so GEM's EndCountryOrArea=India / EndLocation=New Delhi describe the unbuilt, aspirational extent of the historic IPI concept, while the drawn geometry (ending at Karachi) traces the real, discussed Pakistani branch. This reads as a scope/extent mismatch between the row's Start/End columns (full historic tri-national concept) and the digitized geometry (Pakistani Karachi branch only) -- not a coordinate error, and not something to 'fix' by moving the endpoint. Status/ownership/cost already researched elsewhere per brief and not re-litigated here; no new coordinates proposed.
